en.title: Longest Log Whose Maximum User Frequency Matches the Global Baseline
en.description:
Among the users appearing in the whole array, let f be the minimum number of occurrences. Find the maximum length of a contiguous subarray in which the highest user occurrence count is exactly f; it does not require every user in the subarray to have the same frequency.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site; missing numeric bounds and recoveries of source typos are all stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by the user IDs; complete original bounds 1≤n≤300000, 1≤ID≤1000000000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 8; 3; 3. These answers were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: First compute f, then use a sliding window that keeps every user's count ≤f, and also maintain the number of users whose count is exactly f; update the longest length only when that number is non-zero.
